claims.wording: TidyBar is a macOS menu-bar disk cleaner made by Wirecore GmbH in Germany, with official homepage tidy.bar.
The vendor lists macOS 14 Sonoma or later and a universal Apple Silicon/Intel app, described as notarized.
claims.excerpt: TidyBar runs on macOS 14 (Sonoma) and later, on both Apple Silicon and Intel. It's a universal, notarized app.
claims.conditions: Vendor disclosure only; no DMG, signature or hardware test. Windows/Linux support not verified or claimed.

claims.wording: The latest listed changelog version is v1.0.2 dated July 1, 2026; the site says updates use Sparkle.
claims.supportingPassage: v1.0.2 / July 1, 2026 / disk-space checks now run off the main thread.
claims.conditions: Do not call this an independently verified installed/latest downloadable build or adopt speed claims as measurements.

claims.wording: Scanning is free; deletions require a paid licence advertised at $25 once, plus applicable checkout tax, with no subscription and a 30-day money-back guarantee.
claims.excerpt: The price is a one-time payment of $25 (plus any applicable tax shown at checkout); there is no subscription.
claims.supportingPassage: Scanning is free; a paid license is required to perform deletions. We offer a 30-day money-back guarantee
claims.conditions: Dollar symbol as published; explicit ISO currency not stated in retained TidyBar terms. Do not silently label USD, invent device count, or imply refund/payment/activation was tested. Homepage says future major version may be an optional discounted upgrade.

claims.wording: Purchase grants a personal, non-exclusive, non-transferable licence with updates within the purchased version; Gumroad is merchant of record.
claims.excerpt: Upon purchase you receive a personal, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use TidyBar, including updates within the purchased version.
claims.conditions: Commercial restricted licence, not verified open source. No lifetime-all-major-versions or device-seat promise.

claims.wording: The homepage advertises a drill-in disk treemap, large files, duplicates, an uninstaller, snapshots and project cleanup.
claims.excerpt: One app for caches, big files, duplicates, app leftovers, snapshots, and developer build junk.
claims.conditions: Feature names only; not full disk coverage, complete leftovers removal, safe snapshots, accuracy, performance or parity proof.

claims.wording: The vendor describes Developer mode discovering node_modules, DerivedData, target/, .next and virtual environments across chosen project roots, with size/age review and user selection.
claims.excerpt: shows each with its size and age, lets you pick what to remove
claims.supportingPassage: It won't descend into a matched folder or touch anything outside your chosen roots.
claims.conditions: Documented behavior, not a tested traversal boundary. Regeneration depends on preserved source/manifests, available dependencies/toolchains and network. Do not reproduce or run the bulk rm example.

claims.wording: The vendor says removed project items go to Trash, while its terms make the user responsible for reviewing deletion and keeping backups.
claims.excerpt: TidyBar moves removed items to the Trash so they can be recovered; however, you are responsible for reviewing what you delete and for keeping your own backups.
claims.conditions: Not a recovery guarantee or immediately freed-space claim. Snapshot-thinning mechanics and its relationship to blanket Trash language are unverified; exclude that safety generalization.

claims.wording: The press kit says no telemetry, no account and no Full Disk Access required; these are vendor statements about the app, not our network or permissions audit.
claims.excerpt: No telemetry, no account, no Full Disk Access required.
claims.conditions: Do not turn this into all-offline licensing or zero website tracking. Website policy describes server logs, Rybbit, consent-based Meta Pixel and Gumroad purchase processing. Coverage of protected files and activation network requirements unverified.

claims.wording: The press kit permits its screenshot images in coverage of TidyBar.
claims.excerpt: Click to open full size. Free to use in coverage of TidyBar.
claims.conditions: Permission applies to editorial coverage assets, not all brand uses, UI modification, endorsement or source-code licensing.

claims.wording: Breathing Room is a free Apache-2.0 macOS preview identified as 0.1.0-preview.1, for macOS 13+ with Apple Silicon/Intel packaging; it requires Python 3.10+ for inventory/legacy scripts and is not Developer ID signed or notarized.
claims.excerpt: Apple Development signed, not Developer ID signed or notarized.
claims.conditions: RELEASE_NOTES lines 3–10, 24, 32–46; README 64–72; native config version. Physical Intel and clean-machine behavior untested; no instruction to disable protections.

claims.wording: Breathing Room documents category/app/project/folder storage exploration, grouped process CPU/memory and activity history; source implements constrained local cleanup and exact saved approvals for daily care.

claims.conditions: README 76–128 and capabilities source references; source presence is not distributed-binary parity. Sampled writes/inferred ownership are not causal proof. Optional automatic Ruff-cache mode is a qualified exception to per-action approval; daily care requires running app.

workflowArticle.title: Review old project build folders before cleaning your Mac
workflowArticle.primaryIntent: Help a Mac developer decide which inactive-project artifacts can be rebuilt before selecting cleanup candidates, using TidyBar's size/age list as a documented example, not a generic app ranking.
workflowArticle.descriptionBrief: Start with regeneration evidence, not folder size or age. Explain selected-root scanning and selective review, separating generated output from unknown or irreplaceable data; no cleanup was tested for this article.
workflowArticle.conclusion: Use TidyBar's documented project review when the job is selecting old artifacts under known roots; investigate recurrence separately rather than assuming another one-click sweep fixes growth.
outline: Lead then official Project Cleanup image
Choose an owned project root and distinguish source from generated candidates
Check preserved manifests, toolchain/dependency availability and rebuild/download cost; age is a clue, not permission
Review individual paths and selections; Trash is not a backup or immediately freed space
If growth returns, compare a one-off artifact list with Breathing Room's documented storage/activity investigation, disclosing we build it
Show labelled Breathing Room Space browser preview; limitations and concise comparison link
workflowArticle.interactionPass: Hand off a local decision checklist: active project? reproducible dependencies available? any manually edited/generated-only originals? known rebuild cost? backup verified? Unknown or no stops selection. No filesystem access, automatic deletion or savings estimator; not implemented in this research job.
workflowArticle.uniquenessBoundary: Not another node_modules deletion-command tutorial or renamed general cleaner comparison. Focus on item-level rebuild-evidence triage using age/size controls. Source guide's blanket safe/recoverable wording and bulk deletion command are not copied. Check slug/intent collisions before drafting within the separately assigned site scope.
workflowArticle.wordCount: Earned length, typically 900–1800; no padding, artificial FAQ, measured-savings anecdote or mandatory runnable cleanup demo.
